title: f.e.a.r. 3
text: I rate the game F.E.A.R. 3 4/5. Good. This is a fairly impressive FPS game which is designed to be played either as a single player game or entirely as a co-operative game. The plot supports the co-op mode very, very well. While it has some detractors, there is far more to like about this action game than to dislike if you don't mind incredibly violent, occasionally creepy, generally dark games which focus on the family histories of psychotic telepaths. +Wraps up the previous two FEAR games (and the add-ons for each) very, very well with nearly no loose ends while still leaving the way open for yet another sequel if anyone cares to bother to create one without feeling like it has a cliff-hanger ending. +While generally this is not a very creepy game (just bloody and horrific) the game does have its moments (particularly picking your way through the haunted houses in the suburbia section of the game). +The sound and the use of the sound, from the ambient sounds of creaking wood or running feet in another room to the loud gunshots are almost uniformly outstanding. Only the grenades and explosions seemed a little muffled. +Good voice acting though enemies often did end up saying fairly repetitive things during combat and one soldier often sounded like another. +Great between level movie scenes. +Interesting (though often disjointed feeling) plot. +Outstanding and shockingly impressive graphics (the bullet time mode and effects is very well done) Great lighting effects and use of shadows as well. +The two playable characters have interesting and different abilities (but playing as the Ghostly Fettel is much, much easier than playing as the flesh and blood Point Man). +Interesting and varied environments. +This game's plot causes all of the add-on packs to become canonical. +Highly replayable game with two different endings (depending on which character you use and/or if playing in cooperative multiplayer mode, who did better on all of the previous missions. FEAR 3 is Possibly one of the best cooperative FPS gaming experiences ever designed. +Excellent enemy AI and enemy variety. +Outstanding Mech battle sequences. +Your character can only pick up two guns at a time and 3 grenades of each of the 3 types causing for much more intense combat situations and requiring you to make more complex tactical choices. +Excellent controls which support five-button gaming mice. +/- Incredibly violent (and playing one of the character's this violence will often be seen in slow bullet-time motion in painfully exquisite detail. Definitely not a good game for the weak minded or easily influenced or previously disturbed. This game contains particularly disturbing situations and images throughout. -Not extremely creepy throughout. Mostly just bloody and horrific. -This game could have used longer between level cutscenes to flesh out the plot further. -Uneven difficulty. The game is fairly difficult for the point man character but much, much easier for the ghostly Fettel character. -In single player mode the other character vanishes (which, in terms of the plot, makes some sense if you are playing the flesh and blood character but not so well if you are playing the ghost). The game should have included an AI controlled character to assist you when in the playing single player mode to stand-in for an actual person particularly as the game's design and difficulty seems to occasionally forget that you might be playing the game by yourself causing some battle situations to be extremely difficult and possibly even frustrating even on the easier (recruit) difficulty. -The plot will be difficult for newcomers to understand. This game's plot does a very poor job of standing on its own and is clearly intended for those who had played not just the first two games but possibly all of the add-on packs as well. -Relatively short game with only 2 endings. -Fairly linear gameplay and level design. The mech battle sequences, while well done and very atmospheric are particularly linear. -This game has irritating HUD indicators. Text telling you to reload if your clip is not totally full. Stupid on-screen crosshairs that you cannot turn off. -Mediocre music throughout which succeeds only in setting the right tone but fails to be truly catchy or very interesting.

title: f.e.a.r. 3
text: F.E.A.R 3 was developed by Day 1 Studios instead of Monolith Productions and is published by WB Interactive Entertainment. As development house changed, so did F.E.A.R as it became like Call of Duty rip-off. Most people hated this, but to be honest. This game isn't awful and if you look at previous game (F.E.A.R 2: Project Origin), Day 1 Studios actually improved some aspects but unfortunately made some things worse, which is why we never got another F.E.A.R after the third installment. I should mention that it has been a long time since i've played co-op in this game and I haven't tried Fettel playthrough, but I've gathered some information about it, so I know what it offers. I haven't played any multiplayer matches but even if I would've, there most likely wouldn't be any matches. So here are my thoughts: + F.E.A.R 2 had worse A.I than in F.E.A.R but in F.E.A.R 3 A.I acts pretty similar compared to the first game, though it is hard to say if they are better or worse. Most people would've praised this aspect if only maps were more open. + Fettel playthrough: You can possess enemies and use their equipment, including tougher enemy variants and also use some sort of blast that knocks your enemies down. It offers some replay value if you want to play more. + Some story and gameplay ideas are actually interesting. I could go into detail in comments if you want to know more. + Melee is actually viable option unlike in other games where you sometimes strangely miss melee strikes. + Guns feel great, espcially in bullet time. + Sound design + Pretty stable and loading times are quick. * The game takes weapons away from you multiple times but atleast it happens everytime interval ends so it is expected. * Co-op missions: * Pretty boring level system, but it's functional and achieving challenges is useful and somewhat enjoyable. * Health regen is another thing from other shooters but due to it there doesn't seem to be any unfair moments. You know like, melee strikes and going to cover and all. If you disagree, it's fine. - Very bland look. The game also hasn't dated well in graphics department. - Lack of dark areas and lighting effects are dissapointing. - Two weapon limit. This would be fine if previous games didn't allow to carry three weapons (four in F.E.A.R 2) - Lack of weapons. There could've been more. - No ability to blind fire from cover despite the fact that enemies can do this. - Why reveal Point Man's face. First game didn't reveal it, because Point Man was YOU instead of some random generic white guy. - - Alma screams. They are not scary, but annoying. - Level design: I don't know if it was Day 1 Studios or WB's idea but I wish game publishers would avoid COD style levels. They are limited and offer no exploration value. They also make artificial barrier, which include invisible walls, unrealistically blocked off areas and prevents you from backtracking by locking doors behind you. - Hallucination and forced walking-sequences. ♥♥♥♥ them, they are not immersive and makes you feel like game controls your character instead of you controlling it. - This game is FEAR, but it's not scary at all. Maybe one or two times I got spooked but thats it. I've put this game into non-recommended status, because I think whether it is worth your time is up to you. I do think that this game is slightly better than F.E.A.R 2: Project Origin. Devs made changes that are a lot worse but for some reason, I enjoyed this more than 2. A lot of negatives and positives. I guess 5/10 would be pretty accurate rating for this game. Offers some fun (especially in Co-op) but as F.E.A.R game, it's really bad. If you like F.E.A.R (2005) and F.E.A.R 2: Project Origin, I honestly don't know if you are going to like this or not. Some people like F.E.A.R 2: Project Origin more and some people like F.E.A.R 3 more. I'll leave this entirely up to you. If I missed something or you want me to add something important to my review, leave some feedback in the comment section below.

text: After a rough start with compatability issues on the PC I've finaly duggin to this game.  I can only say they have done it again.  This game is absolutly amazing the new graphic are a major improvment and fluid compared to Fallout Vegas.  They have a new crafting system allowing you to use every little thing you can find and "scrap" it for parts.  In addition to building items the new system also allows for making your own buildings.  Constructing entire forts and set up turrets, traps, furnature, and decorations.  The change in crafting system has also made a change in the weapon system not the least of which being no more durability on weapons.  The new system allows you to customize weapons even make up your own names for them.  Over all the improvements made to the game are almost all positive making this game the new Gem of the Fallout Dynasty.

title: fallout: new vegas
text: Fallout: New Vegas is the fourth Fallout we should have gotten, but sadly we got the garbage pile that was just Fallout 4 instead. But that's another review for another day. Thanks to mods and the modding community, this game can be changed to make it look like it was developed and released in 2017. To bring this game up to speed with current hardware, I'd recommend getting the following mods from the Nexus website: Please note that in order to utilize these mods properly, you must use the Fallout New Vegas Script Extender. Fallout New Vegas is literally the best of the best experience when it comes to open world first person shooters with RPG elements in it. Obsidian literally fixed EVERYTHING that was wrong with Bethesda's release of Fallout 3, and even surpasses Bethesda's latest title, Fallout 4, in many ways. Traits are back from the first two Fallouts and some mods add even the original traits from the first two games. Speech checks are now based on a specific number rather than a percentage chance so that if you want to win speech checks, you HAVE to build your character around charisma a bit. You can't completely ignore charisma anymore by reloading a save, but instead if you want to be able to convince someone, you have to actually level up your speech skill or you don't pass the speech check. Energy weapons actually feel powerful enough that it's now a skill worth investing points into. I could write an essay on why New Vegas surpasses Bethesda's failure of a game that is Fallout 4, but if you buy this game, you'll instantly realize just how much better this game is compared to Bethesda's releases and how this game hearkens back to the development and gameplay style of Fallout 1 and 2. If Fallout 5 turns out to be developed by Obsidian and retains the proper RPG elements that New Vegas is known and loved for, then I will be very happy to buy it day one. Get the Ultimate Edition. It's worth every dollar and some of the mods I mentioned require all the DLC regardless. Worth playing and replaying.
